synopsis: Pre-registration is a core control against result-driven analysis: before hardware arrives, the program should fix acceptance criteria, strata, confidence levels and stopping rules, with the statistical plan scheduled for October 2026 to mid-2027 [f6956, f7363]. Release-rate claims must use a frozen stratified random sample drawn from the declared operating-domain distribution before tuning and never used for tuning; discovery, estimation and regression tests must remain separate [f14131, f133]. Statistical safeguards include pre-declared binomial intervals when misses occur, fixed sequential stopping rules, and predefined primary claims with multiplicity methods where many claims must hold together [f6891, f14225, f7486]. The recommended pilot is a difficult thin vertical slice predicted blind against pre-registered criteria, with a proposed 10–30 physical test points and metrics such as detection-range error, stopping-distance error and false-negative agreement [f9485, f9917, f9919]. Evidence supporting pre-declared progression criteria and locked metrics comes from health and social research, so its transfer to engineering remains an analogy rather than direct proof; few sensor-realism studies define acceptance thresholds before testing [f9903, f9904, f4839]. A late change in sensor modalities can invalidate the frozen plan, requiring sensor-dependent strata to be re-derived and the sample redrawn, consuming validation time [f7490, f7491, f14303].
